Hi Kimberly / Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo today — it was helpful to see Redwood's runtime and the streaming behavior for long notes. Quick synth of where we landed on our side and a small sample attached for your team to use in a pilot.

What we care most about: 
- Accuracy and extractive fidelity when summarizing very long visit notes (3–6k tokens typical, some up to ~25k tokens).
- Avoiding subtle contradictions (patient meds / allergies) after summarization.
- Predictable cost / latency for a production workflow (we expect ~40k notes / mo).

Questions we flagged:
1) Is there a recommended model class for fidelity-first long-context summarization?
2) Does Redwood offer a graceful fallback when input exceeds model window (chunking + merge vs. 32k models)?
3) Any public benchmark or prompt sets you recommend we run against our sample?

Attached: mednotebook_sample_notes.csv (200 rows — redacted).

Next step: Can your team propose a short evaluation plan (1 week, up to 1k notes) and a pilot estimate?

—Laura

Hi Laura — great to meet you and thanks for the sample. High-level recap and a recommended plan below. I added Rishi and Ben from our evaluation team to scope an ops + model checklist.

Recap / primary goals (as I heard them):
- High factual fidelity for clinical summaries; low tolerance for contradictions.
- Bulk: ~40k notes/mo; initial pilot: 1k notes.
- Some notes exceed 8k tokens and a portion approach 25k.

Immediate recommendation (summary):
1) Baseline model: amber-33b-32k (32k context, quantized variant) — best tradeoff for fidelity vs. cost for now.
2) Fallback pipeline: shard -> overlap-merge -> final refinement prompt (see attachment km_longctx_promptset_v1.txt).
3) Eval metrics: Rouge-L, QA-factuality (extract true/false checks), hallucination rate (entity mismatch), and latency P95.

Why amber-33b-32k?
- 32k window avoids most truncation for your sample, preserves KV cache locality, and reduces complexity vs maintaing chunk+merge only.
- Quantized build keeps unit cost reasonable while preserving output quality; we can trial an FP16 baseline if you want a small fidelity uplift.

Pilot scope (proposed):
- Duration: 7 business days.
- Dataset: 1k notes sampled by length buckets (short, mid, long).
- Deliverables: benchmark report (benchmarks_longdoc_summarization_results_YYYYMMDD.pdf), prompt set, runbook, and an ops estimate.

Attachments I included: km_longctx_promptset_v1.txt (prompt templates + merge strategy), initial eval script. Ben will follow with technical eval notes + a cost estimate.

Next step: are you available for a 30m alignment on Thu 14th or Mon 18th? I can walk through the pilot plan and we can lock in the scope.

Thanks —

Adding some technical specifics / pilot acceptance criteria so the sales-side can include them in the action plan.

1) Hallucination metric (practical):
- Run QA-extraction on gold records (patient meds, allergies, diagnoses). For each note, compute entity-precision: (# correct entities in summary) / (# entities in gold). Pilot acceptance: entity-precision >= 0.99 across sample (tunable).
- Complement with answer-consistency checks: sample N QA pairs and compute F1; if mean F1 drops below 0.92 we flag a quality regression.

2) Truncation & fallback behavior:
- Runtime options: A) Route to 32k model variant when input_size <= 32k. B) For >32k, a preprocessor can chunk with 400-token overlap + summarize each chunk + chain-merge and then a final consolidation prompt.
- We recommend "auto-route" for <32k inputs and preprocessor+merge for >32k to control hallucination risk. Runtime can attach provenance traces for each chunk so you can audit source spans.

3) Metrics & telemetry to capture during pilot:
- P95 and P99 latency, mean tokens per request, cost per summarized note, entity-precision, QA-F1, top-k logprob distributions for key entities, and per-token cache hit rates.

4) Evaluation artifacts I attached:
- benchmarks_longdoc_summarization_results_20270114.pdf (sample run across 300 notes) — highlights where chunk+merge lost factuality vs. single 32k model.
- eval_script_run.sh (link in Drive) and a short Jupyter notebook for QA-based checks.

5) Pilot cost (ballpark for 1k notes):
- Amber-33b-32k quantized: ~$1,800 for the run (compute + storage + telemetry) — we will provide a line-item breakdown in the action plan.

6) Data residency / retention:
- We can run the pilot in our US-only cluster and purge logs after 30 days; scrubbed logs (non-PHI) can be retained for 90 days if helpful for debugging.

Attachments / links: benchmarks_longdoc_summarization_results_20270114.pdf, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b_longctx_eval_prompts

Happy to refine thresholds — once we agree on acceptance gates we'll schedule the Mon 18th 30m slot.
